st.headline: Apple overtakes Nvidia to become world’s most valuable company
st.teaser: This is the first time Apple has overtaken Nvidia since briefly doing so in late July.
fullText: Apple reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company on Oct 30, taking the mantle from Nvidia as investors seek the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending.
Shares of Apple fell 1.2% on Oct 30, resulting in a market capitalisation of US$5.03 trillion (S$6.4 trillion), while Nvidia sank 4.2% to close with a valuation of US$4.93 trillion.
This is the first time Apple has overtaken Nvidia since briefly doing so in late July.

The Oct 30 sell-off came as a number of major technology companies disappointed with their results, including Intel and Amazon, which followed similarly disappointing reports from Alphabet and Meta Platforms, among others.
The reports renewed concerns about the outlook for AI spending, something Apple has largely foregone.

Fears that heavy spending on AI computing infrastructure will not pay off have helped make Apple, which has kept a lid on capital expenditures, by far the best performing of the Magnificent Seven tech giants in 2026.
Its shares are up 27% in 2026, more than twice the gain of second-place Nvidia, which is a key beneficiary of AI spending.
The outlays have become so large that companies like Alphabet and Amazon have seen their free cash flow turn negative, forcing them to increasingly turn to debt markets for funding.
Meanwhile, rising interest rates are raising the cost of borrowing.
Apple, by contrast, is projected to see its free cash flow climb 38% to US$142 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended on Sept 30.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index fell 6.7% in October, its worst month since March 2025.

CoreWeave and Nebius Group, data centre owners that offer AI computing services, have dropped more than 30% in October. With the Oct 30 collapse, Intel lost more than 45% in October, its biggest ever one-month drop in data compiled by Bloomberg going back more than 40 years. BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some scraping
cna.teaser: Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every bot that crawls the web to collect data, but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardised instruction that's recognised and honoured.
fullText: SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday (Oct 31) to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being scraped to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every bot that crawls the web to collect data, but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardised instruction that's recognised and honoured by any AI company that adopts the protocol.
The solution will not fully take effect for months, though.

Microsoft will implement it beginning Feb 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out "in the coming months", while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has "already started" rolling it out.

In December 2023, the Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft for allegedly using millions of its articles without authorization or payment to train ChatGPT. The two tech companies are invoking an exception to copyright law known as fair use.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.

The new setting will apply only to future training of models but does not prevent bots from crawling otherwise, and content scraping will be allowed by default until the setting is changed by a publisher, Microsoft said in a blog post.
Opting out of AI training could reduce the chances that a publisher's content will surface in AI apps and experiences, Microsoft and Google said in separate blog posts.

"We believe creating a common signal that conveys such preferences to multiple providers at once is an important step. And we look forward to working with other AI companies on the standards and their implementation across the industry," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote on X, conveying his support for the effort.

listening.title: Singapore Expands Green Corridor Network to Enhance Biodiversity
listening.transcript: Singapore has officially announced the expansion of its Nature Park Network, adding over fifty hectares of connected green spaces across the island. The initiative aims to enhance urban biodiversity while offering residents greater access to recreational trails. Officials emphasized that seamlessly linking these habitats will protect native wildlife species amidst ongoing urban redevelopment.

economistArticle.title: The Leadership Vacuum at the European Central Bank
paras: When Christine Lagarde steps down from the helm of the European Central Bank, she will leave behind an institution grappling with unprecedented structural headwinds. The Eurozone economy, long plagued by sluggish growth and fragile fiscal cohesion, faces an increasingly volatile macroeconomic landscape. Negotiating this treacherous terrain will require a delicate balancing act that her successor may struggle to maintain.

High interest rates, deployed to tame post-pandemic inflation, have begun to sap vitality from core industrial sectors, particularly in Germany and France. Meanwhile, public debt levels across southern member states remain perilously elevated, leaving national treasuries with limited room for counter-cyclical spending. The Central Bank finds itself caught between the imperative to quell persistent service-sector inflation and the urgent need to cushion faltering output.

Geopolitical friction further complicates the policy calculus. Rising trade barriers and supply-chain fragmentation threaten to erode Europe's export-oriented economic model. Should a new wave of protectionist tariffs emerge from Washington or Beijing, the monetary authority in Frankfurt will have few conventional tools left to insulate the bloc from external shocks.

Consequently, the individual chosen to succeed Lagarde will assume command during a crucial juncture. Without decisive reform and institutional realignment, the central bank risks being overburdened by political expectations it cannot realistically fulfill. The task ahead is not merely technical monetary management, but the delicate preservation of monetary union itself.
economistArticle.cn: 当克里斯蒂安·拉加德卸任欧洲中央银行行长一职时，她留下的将是一个正在与前所未有的结构性逆风作斗争的机构。长期受增长缓慢和财政凝聚力脆弱困扰的欧元区经济，正面临着日益动荡的宏观经济环境。应对这一艰难局面需要维持微妙的平衡，而她的继任者可能难以维系。为了遏制疫情后的通胀而实施的高利率，已开始削弱核心工业部门（尤其是德国和法国）的活力。与此同时，南部成员国的公共债务水平仍处于危险的高位，使各国财政部逆周期支出的空间十分有限。中央银行发现自己处于两难境地：一边是遏制持续的服务业通胀的必要举措，另一边则是缓冲摇摇欲坠的产出的迫切需求。地缘政治摩擦进一步使政策考量复杂化。日益高企的贸易壁垒和供应链碎片化威胁着欧洲出口导向型经济模式。如果华盛顿或北京掀起新一轮保护主义关税浪潮，法兰克福的货币当局将几乎没有传统工具来保护该贸易集团免受外部冲击。因此，被选来接替拉加德的人选将在关键时刻接掌大权。如果没有决断性的改革和机构重组，中央银行可能会因政治期望负担过重，而这些期望是它在现实中无法实现的。前面的任务不仅是技术性的货币管理，而是精心维护货币联盟本身。

gems.s: The Central Bank finds itself caught between the imperative to quell persistent service-sector inflation and the urgent need to cushion faltering output.
gems.why: Uses a elegant 'caught between A and B' contrast structure paired with parallel noun phrases to vividly portray a policy dilemma. 此句使用对称的‘夹在A与B之间’对比结构，配合强有力的平行名词短语，极其生动地展现了央行面临的政策两难困境。
